subject.title: Codex bootstrap accounting misses memory_recall and doctor is harness-blind

question: Should Codex bootstrap accounting recognize a generic plugin-declared memory-routing capability, or is `memory_recall` an intentional fixed member of the native Codex memory-tool contract?
rationale: The report spans core Codex harness behavior and plugin-provided tools; choosing a one-off tool-name allowlist versus a declared capability determines the durable compatibility boundary.

options.title: Use a declared capability
options.body: Define and consume a generic memory-routing capability so Codex accounting and doctor share one plugin-compatible contract.

options.title: Recognize memory_recall directly
options.body: Add `memory_recall` beside the existing recognized names only if it is a stable, documented Codex tool contract.

options.title: Retain current routing
options.body: Keep the bounded injection behavior if the current Codex harness intentionally does not route plugin memory tools natively.

recommendation.title: Use a declared capability
recommendation.body: Define and consume a generic memory-routing capability so Codex accounting and doctor share one plugin-compatible contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest available history signal is prior work on Codex context/runtime behavior.
